residency.test: Full tax liability arises on taking up residence, or after six months of continuous stay. Simply having a home available in Denmark and staying there for work can be enough.
residency.researcher_scheme: The expat scheme taxes qualifying researchers and highly paid employees at 27% plus AM-bidrag (an effective 32.84%) for up to seven years, subject to a minimum salary requirement.
residency.note: Danish residence rules are triggered easily. Buying or renting a year-round dwelling is often the decisive fact.

headline.am_bidrag: 8% labour market contribution off the top of gross salary

local_tax.name: Kommuneskat (municipal tax)
local_tax.note: national average; ranges from about 23.4% in Rudersdal to 26.3% in Langeland

personal_allowance.name: Personfradrag
personal_allowance.note: applied here as a deduction; Denmark technically grants it as a credit at the bottom-bracket plus municipal rate

surcharges.name: Topskat (top-bracket tax)
surcharges.note: charged on personal income after AM-bidrag; from 2026 this splits into a middle and a top bracket

capital_gains.shares: 27% up to 67,500 of share income (135,000 for couples), 42% above
capital_gains.property: gains on your own home are exempt under the parcelhusreglen if you have lived there
capital_gains.other_capital_income: net capital income is taxed with other income, with a separate ceiling of 42%
capital_gains.note: Denmark taxes some unrealised gains on foreign investment funds and pension assets annually

quirks: AM-bidrag comes off the top before anything else, so the headline marginal rate of about 55.9% for top-bracket taxpayers already includes it.
The tax ceiling caps the combined bottom, top and municipal rate at 52.07%, but AM-bidrag and church tax sit outside the ceiling.
Church tax of roughly 0.7% is charged automatically to members of the Danish National Church; you must actively opt out.
The 27% expat scheme has a strict minimum salary requirement checked every month, and one month below the threshold can disqualify you retroactively.
Preliminary income assessment (forskudsopgørelse) drives your monthly withholding. Updating it when your circumstances change is how Danes avoid a large bill in March.

reporting.who_must_file: Everyone receives an annual statement (årsopgørelse) that is generated automatically. You must correct it if anything is missing - most notably foreign income, property abroad and share transactions.

deadlines.what: Deadline to correct the annual statement for most individuals
Deadline for taxpayers with foreign income or self-employment
Preliminary income assessment (forskudsopgørelse) for the following year is published
Residual tax paid by this date carries a lower interest surcharge

forms.name: Information form for those with income not reported automatically
Preliminary income assessment driving monthly withholding
Application for the researcher/expat tax scheme

documents_to_collect: The årsopgørelse, which already contains salary, interest, mortgage and Danish share income
Foreign income, foreign pension and foreign property details - none of this is pre-filled
Documentation of commuting distance for the befordringsfradrag, which is generous over long distances
Union fees and unemployment insurance (A-kasse) contributions, both deductible
Records of any share purchases and sales through foreign brokers

penalties.late_correction: an estimated assessment (taksation) plus a fee of about 200
penalties.underreporting: penalties from one to two times the evaded tax, with criminal liability above thresholds
penalties.interest: a non-deductible surcharge on residual tax, higher after 1 July

warnings: The personal allowance is applied as a deduction rather than as Denmark's actual tax credit, which slightly changes results.
The 52.07% tax ceiling is not enforced by this model; very high incomes may be marginally overstated.
Church tax is excluded. Add roughly 0.7% of taxable income for members.
